alternate_valid_findings: A material distinct skip/xfail state or reporting gap can be accepted when traced to a production branch and not covered by current assertions.

A precise missing skipif combination can be assessed independently, but absence of that spelling alone does not establish an unprotected shared normalization path: the fixed assertion covers the same skipped_by_mark normalization branch.

contracts.contract: --runxfail forces running/reporting xfail-marked tests as though not marked and makes imperative xfail have no effect.
runxfail option is xfail-specific; mark skip reports are normalized to the test item definition.
Production runtest report creation is passed through the skipping hook.
Terminal summaries display locations from skipped reports.

limitations: Source-only: no target imports, tests, discovery, build, install, Docker, or execution occurred.
Each packet is a bounded selection of complete raw upstream files, not a runnable checkout. External dependencies and unrelated modules are absent.
Contracts, production callers, related tests and root test configuration are visible. Authoritative history and exact fixed-parent relations remain sealed from auditors.
Each packet is internally from one exact upstream commit. No authored target code, excerpt substitutions, injected comments, issue summaries, diffs, or targeted failure prompts are in packets.
Fixed controls deliberately include upstream regression assertions, while pre-fix twins naturally do not; the comparison uses identical packets across skill arms.
Public historical cases may have appeared in model training. Prior familiarity cannot be excluded, and packets disclose project identity through their unmodified contents.
Blinding is an instructed filesystem boundary, not an OS-enforced sandbox. Auditors must receive only one staged packet and must not browse history, sibling packets, rubric, or oracle.
Only the permitted prior protocol was inspected for exclusions. Prior audit outputs and the revised skill were not read.
Control means protected against the declared historical interaction, not proven defect-free or immune to other material test gaps.
oracle_challenges: The targeted new regression explicitly spells mark.skip, not every mark.skipif variant or plugin report type. Do not claim complete marking coverage.
Other hook wrappers and custom items can alter reports. Claims depending on omitted third-party behavior should remain unresolved unless the supplied source proves the necessary contract.
protected_evidence: src/_pytest/skipping.py:295 onward uses an independent if for skip location normalization after the xfail-policy chain.
testing/test_skipping.py:238-264 test_xfail_run_with_skip_mark parametrizes both -rs and -rs --runxfail, checks the exact user test path and line, and checks one skipped result.
The generated test has @pytest.mark.skip and a failing body; this assertion genuinely exercises the mark/option/reporting interaction rather than inspecting a helper in isolation.
protected_false_alarms: Claiming --runxfail still prevents location normalization for ordinary skip marks because the normalization is elif-connected to that option.
Claiming tests never combine --runxfail and mark.skip or never assert the user location in that combination.
scope: Skip and expected-failure marking, execution policy and result reporting.
target: Xfail execution policy does not bypass normalization of skip-mark report locations.
